walkthroughs.body_html:
Some historians stress the violence of the Harrying of the North in 1069-70 — thousands starved.

Others see William as a strong organiser whose Domesday Book and castles built lasting order. Both interpretations use the same events but weight them differently.

Elizabeth (reigned 1558-1603) faced threats from Spain, Mary Queen of Scots and religious division.

She survived the Spanish Armada in 1588 and kept a fragile religious settlement. But she relied heavily on Parliament for money — power was not absolute.

walkthroughs.h2: Why the Civil War still matters
walkthroughs.body_html:
The execution of Charles I in 1649 showed Parliament could remove a king.

After the 1688 Glorious Revolution, England moved toward constitutional monarchy — kings ruled with Parliament's consent. This long-term change began in the medieval and early modern struggles you've studied.
